text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The Danish bond market could face falling prices when the U.S. Fed as expected raises its interest rates this spring, several Danish banks say.

--- Danish Social Minister Karen Jespersen wants to set up a new central anti-violence centre with groups of trained social workers on standby to move into areas where youth violence breaks out at short notice.

--- Danish doctors warn against a Justice Ministry proposal to keep DNA and information files on serious criminals and non-convicted defendants, on the grounds that innocent people will find themselves involuntarily registered by the authorities.
--- 61 percent of all Danes want the results of the European Union's intergovernmental conference to be submitted to a national referendum, a new survey shows.
--- Denmark's biggest banks are to initiate new massive staff cuts in 1997 and 1998, shedding 1,400 jobs this year alone.
